narrativeProgression.description: Steve Reick acknowledges the new funding model passed by the state legislature.
Steve Reick explains how the model establishes funding levels based on school needs and various benchmarks.
Steve Reick clarifies that the model takes into account factors like class size, ESL students, and special needs to determine funding.
Steve Reick points out that the model is expected to benefit Harvard financially.
Harmilda asks about the availability of funds for the additional funding required by the model.
Steve Reick admits it's a valid concern, revealing the state legislature's allocation of an additional $350 million for the model.
Steve Reick acknowledges the reliance on economic growth to provide the necessary funding.
Steve Reick emphasizes the state's constitutional responsibility to fund education and the ongoing effort to fulfill that obligation.

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Hello everyone, welcome back to Hang with Harmila. A special day for us here is we're with State Representative Steve Reich.
There's a lot of buzz in educational circles about the new evidence based model of funding and that's something new for how our schools are funded.
So we're open Steve can tell us a little bit more about it and what it means for us here in Harvard.
Thank you. We just passed in the State Legislature just passed in the Governor's
signed a bill that changes the way we pay for schools, are supposed to pay for schools here in Illinois.
It establishes a funding level for certain benchmarks that a school should have.
It takes class sizes, ESL students, special needs and puts them all into a formula that says,
okay if you have this many kids in in kindergarten you need you'll get so much funding based upon that number of children.
But the fact is is that the evidence based model stands to help Harvard gain quite a lot of money because
Harvard is in the tier one level of schools which means it's furthest away from
adequacy and the model puts more money into the lower tier schools with the hope of bringing them up toward
adequacy. It quantifies the needs of various school districts. Obviously the thing is will the money be
available in order to make that leap in additional funding? That's a good question. The state legislature is
appropriated an additional $350 million for implementing the the K through 12 or the evidence based model.
We'll see if we get it. Economic growth has to has to provide that but the fact remains is that we're trying to find a way in which
schools can receive the kind of funding from the state of Illinois. The Constitution says
the state's primarily responsible for paying for education. Now we're trying to figure out a way how we step up and actually do that.
Wonderful congratulations to all the legislators who have made that happen and we're excited to see what it means to Harvard and then most importantly to our students who deserve
only the very best. Thanks everyone.

youtube_description:
Harvard Community Unit School District 50 Superintendent Dr. Corey Tafoya talks with State Representative Steve Reick about the new school funding bill for the State of Illinois. SB 1947 is an evidence-based bill intended to provide increased funding and opportunities for Harvard CUSD 50 students.
